notes:
- Every wide shot is zoomed on its people, even one person alone; when two sit too far apart, it zooms out so both stay inside the guardrails, the wall and floor carried on above and below. A wide holds one framing for the whole shot, even when a screen behind the people changes.
- A face counts as a person only when it sits at the top of someone's body, so a face in a video high on the set's screen is never followed.
- A clip keeps the format you chose: when its cuts don't check out they are repaired and the clip remade in the same format, never swapped for Hook Box.
- No cut inside a word or a sentence: a cut that splits speech is undone, an end never trails into the next sentence, and the end of a sentence is never cut while its start plays.
- No quick pause jumps right next to another camera change or in the opening seconds.
- Captions take their spelling, capitals and punctuation from the whole recording (YouTube, LeBron, I), never join two speakers or run across a cut, and never show a stray dash.
- Headline: the title and the yellow line at the sizes you set, in any font (the line never shrinks to unreadable).
- Music: the same song never plays under two of any five clips in a row.
